reasoning_traces.think:
The prediction engine operates under a deterministic, statistical paradigm rather than machine learning. Its core operator is the confidence scoring algorithm, which aggregates multiple market signals—implied probability, line movement, consensus, and market depth—into a single normalized score. This score is then mapped to discrete tiers (PREMIUM/FREE/NOT PUBLISHED) via a threshold rule. The engine avoids AI by relying on fixed formulas and historical calibration instead of adaptive learning. Failure modes include misalignment of consensus with true outcome, insufficient bookmaker depth, or stale historical performance. The system's robustness depends on signal-to-noise ratios in the input data and the stability of market dynamics.
